subject: Re: Performance SLOs — context window, token limits, and latency impact
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, Apr 28, 2027 at 3:10 PM -0700
Subject: Performance SLOs — context window, token limits, and latency impact

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size a short PoC:

- Target latency: you mentioned 200–300ms p95 for user-facing responses when returning ~512 tokens. Please confirm whether that 200–300ms target includes network RTT to your clients or is strictly server-side generation time.
- Concurrency/throughput: you said ~50 concurrent active users at peak with an average of 20 QPS sustained. Is that per-region? Any expected spikes >100 QPS?
- Streaming: you prefer server-sent events (incremental tokens) for progressive rendering; do you need tokens delivered as soon as available (true streaming) or are chunked updates acceptable?
- Context window: you indicated up to 32k tokens of conversation history + a ~4k token document as input in some flows. Is the 32k a hard requirement for initial phase or a long-term target?

Next steps from our side: Rishi will provide an initial performance estimate and call out tradeoffs between model size, quantization, and batching. If you can share a short sample of typical prompts and an export of token size distribution, we can run a small spike against a representative model family.

Attachments: finco_performance_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB) — feels like a helpful source of truth for the PoC.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finco.com>
Date: Thu, Apr 28, 2027 at 4:05 PM -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs — context window, token limits, and latency impact

Thanks Marissa — nice recap. A few clarifications and concrete targets from our side:

- Latency target: 250ms p95 end-to-end for the happy path (UI -> inference -> UI). We understand some of this is network; assume ~50ms average network RTT, so ~200ms server-side generation for a ~512-token answer is our goal.
- Token behavior: typical responses are 300–600 tokens, occasionally up to ~1,200 tokens for long-form summaries. We can cap for PoC at 512 output tokens if needed, but want to understand latency impact when we scale to 1,200 tokens.
- Concurrency & throughput: peak concurrent active users ~50 per region, sustained 20 QPS, with short bursts to ~120 QPS for 30–60s during business-hours resyncs.
- Streaming: we want true streaming (token-by-token or small-chunk streaming) so users see partial results quickly. Starting to display after ~100 tokens is OK, but earlier is better.
- Context window: long-term we want 32k token context (conversation + doc), but for PoC we can limit to 16k to simplify. Important to understand whether model variant changes (e.g., 32k vs 16k) will affect p95 latency materially.

I've attached our requirements spreadsheet. We'll also share a sample of our prompt templates and token distribution by EOD.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of AI Products, FinCo
alex.johnson@finco.com
+1 (617) 555-0189

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Apr 29, 2027 at 9:20 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs — context window, token limits, and latency impact

Alex — great details, thanks. High-level responses and a suggested plan below. TL;DR: context window increases memory and KV-cache pressure but does not linearly increase generation time; output token length and streaming mode are the dominant latency drivers.

Observations / assumptions:
- Model family: throughput & latency numbers below assume a mid-sized causal LLM we commonly use for production (quantized where possible). If you pick a much larger model >30B, numbers will shift.
- Network: we focus on server-side generation times; assume 50ms external RTT as you called out.

Latency impact summary (approximate p95 server-side generation):
- 512 output tokens, 16k context window: ~120–180ms p95 single-request (no batching), depending on GPU instance.
- 512 output tokens, 32k context window: ~140–210ms p95 — ~10–20% uplift due to longer KV cache handling and larger attention state.
- 1,200 output tokens, 16k context: ~300–400ms p95 (longer outputs dominate).

Key tradeoffs and controls:
- Batching: helps throughput but increases tail latency for user-facing single-request flows. For strict p95 SLOs, we recommend small batch windows (5–10ms) or prefer per-request routing to instances optimized for low-latency (dedicated pools).
- Quantization: 4-bit quantization reduces latency and memory, can help support 32k contexts more cheaply with modest accuracy tradeoffs.
- Streaming: with true token streaming we can return partial tokens as they decode — first token latency is typically the same, but perceived latency improves dramatically. For example, start-of-stream for the 512-token case is ~80–120ms, then subsequent tokens stream out. If you require first N tokens quickly, we can tune generation parameters and decoding top-k to prioritize speed.
- Concurrency: for your 20 QPS sustained / 120 QPS bursts, we'd recommend a small dedicated GPU pool sized for peak with autoscale buffers and a fallback policy to a slightly higher-latency tier for overflow.

Suggested next steps (PoC plan):
1) You share sample prompts + token distribution (thanks — looking for the file).
2) We run a spike: simulate 20 QPS sustained and a 120 QPS 60s burst against a 16k context config, measuring p95 and 99.
3) If the 16k PoC looks good, run one 32k variant to measure delta in p95 and resource usage.
4) Deliver a short perf brief (PDF) with recommended model/config and estimated cost/throughput.

I'll attach an initial perf estimate PDF that includes example latency curves and GPU sizing guidance. Also: one immediate ask — can you provide typical average prompt + context byte sizes and the % of requests that will exceed 512 tokens? That will let us choose the right model variant for the PoC.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
